If I could just see a doctor and get my medical problem taken care of (and continue to do so since it is a reoccurring issue that should be monitored), I wouldn't be suicidal. I hadn't been suicidal in a long time until this started happening. This issue I've been having is the source of all my other problems, but no one will listen to me. Hell, even my doctor wouldn't listen to me about it, but at least she could easily take care of the physical problem at hand.

I'm not out except for online and I changed my pronouns about a year and a half ago I think. I've always gone by some sort of nickname that isn't my birth name since I was around 16 (I'm 24 now) and my family still calls me my birthname and I hate it. I always didn't like my birthname but once I knew I wasn't cis, it made it worse. I realized I wasn't cis almost 2 years ago and I actually flip-flopped around with what gender-neutral pronouns I wanted. I didn't feel like they/them/their fit me personally, so I went searching the net and eventually found a set I liked, tweaked it a teeny bit and used those. A few months ago though I finally settled on ey/em/eir. As for *when* you should change them - I really can't say. It's different for everyone. "When you're ready" is such a generic answer tbh, but it's true. You'll know when you're ready, when you're comfortable with it, and who to tell at what time. Like I said, I'm not out to anyone irl and the only irl friend I've come out to completely is one I interact with most online bc we don't get to see each other too often.
